items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: No after Charlie Barnet I went with Gene Krupa’s band.

ctx.x: That’s a black market album you know, from Milano. And I had a friend of mine, I was working at Eddie Condon’s on 54th Street one night, and I saw a friend of mine who was a distributor. Joe Muranyi sent me this, the clarinet player, he sent me this. He said, “I’ve got an album of you and Louis and Tyree.” I said, “what do you mean? Send me the album.” I said I can’t believe this, it’s double album, see? It’s got our pictures inside and everything. But the reason I think they picked Tyree and me was because he…

encore, do something else. You could either do the same thing over, or play another song. So Tyree and I both got big enough hands that he would say do another song. So they figured in Italy, in Milano, they said these guys must be the big stars in the band, because they’re the only ones that did an extra chorus. That’s the only way I can figure it out. Because why would they do that? And that’s a funny story. Was that after Charlie Barnet? No after Charlie Barnet I went with Gene Krupa’s band.
